intervention_label: Direct BAX activator BTSA1 (BAX trigger-site chemical probe)
target_feature_label: TP53 aberration - the apoptotic effector arm sitting below p53
mechanism: BTSA1 binds the N-terminal trigger site of BAX and forces the conformational change that drives BAX translocation and oligomerisation at the outer mitochondrial membrane. Because it engages BAX protein directly, it does not wait on p53 to transcribe PUMA or NOXA.
rationale: Her blasts grew through venetoclax, and Nechiporuk's screen makes TP53 loss on its own enough to produce that phenotype, because the p53 target genes that supply BH3-only activators go missing. A direct BAX activator starts one step below where the wiring is cut. Reyna and colleagues reported activity in CD34+CD38- fractions from high-risk AML, which is the compartment that survived FLAG-IDA here. This is a mechanism argument about where to look, not a treatment: no clinical-grade BAX activator exists.
novelty: No BAX activator has an IND or a registered trial in any indication, and BAX-directed chemistry appears nowhere in trials.jsonl, clinical_evidence.jsonl or preclinical_evidence.jsonl.

key_manuscripts.finding: BTSA1 bound the BAX trigger site, drove BAX-dependent mitochondrial apoptosis in AML lines and primary blasts including CD34+CD38- cells, and suppressed human AML xenografts without overt toxicity. Sensitivity tracked with how much free anti-apoptotic BCL-2 protein was around to re-sequester activated BAX.

Loss of TP53, BAX or PMAIP1 was each sufficient to make AML cells venetoclax-resistant, and the resistant cells leaned on BCL2L1 instead. This is the premise for going after the effector layer rather than the BH3 mimetic layer.

developability: A chemical probe and nothing more. Eight years after the Cancer Cell paper there is still no IND-enabling BAX activator, so reaching this patient would mean starting a medicinal-chemistry program from scratch.
risks: Needs intact BAX protein. If this clone took the BAX-null route to venetoclax resistance, the drug has no substrate at all
Potency is capped by how much free BCL-2 and BCL-xL is available to re-bind activated BAX, so a BCL-xL-high clone would blunt it
BAX is ubiquitous; on-target apoptosis in normal haematopoiesis and gut has never been characterised in humans
No published data in TP53-mutant AML specifically, so the p53-bypass claim is inferred rather than tested
caveats: The in-vivo result comes from a single laboratory and has not been independently reproduced.

intervention_label: 753B, a VHL-recruiting dual BCL-xL/BCL-2 PROTAC degrader
target_feature_label: TP53 aberration with venetoclax failure and compensatory BCL2L1 reliance
mechanism: 753B ties BCL-xL and BCL-2 to the von Hippel-Lindau E3 ligase so both proteins are ubiquitinated and destroyed rather than occupied. Platelets do not express VHL, which is the design trick meant to separate 753B from navitoclax on thrombocytopenia.
rationale: Her disease progressed on venetoclax with a CD34+/CD14-/CD64- non-monocytic phenotype, which argues against the MCL1-driven monocytic escape route and toward the BCL-xL arm that Nechiporuk mapped to TP53/BAX/PMAIP1 loss. Konopleva's group ran 753B against primary AML samples including venetoclax-resistant ones and against AML PDX models. Removing BCL-xL protein rather than blocking its groove also matters if the clone has raised BCL2L1 levels. Nothing here says it would work in her; it says the resistance mechanism and the compound line up.
novelty: DT2216, the BCL-xL-only VHL degrader from the same chemistry, has entered phase 1 and so belongs to trial_screener; 753B has no IND and no registered study, and no BCL-xL-directed agent of any kind appears in the three upstream files.

key_manuscripts.finding: 753B degraded BCL-xL and BCL-2 dose-dependently, cut viability in AML cell lines, primary samples and PDX models, and spared platelets because they lack VHL. It also killed chemotherapy-induced senescent AML cells, which the authors put forward as a separate senolytic benefit.

Venetoclax-resistant AML cells arising from TP53, BAX or PMAIP1 loss shifted their survival dependence onto BCL2L1. That shift is the reason a BCL-xL-inclusive agent is worth scanning for after venetoclax failure.

developability: Academic compound with no sponsor-declared IND. The VHL-sparing concept has been carried into the clinic by DT2216, so the regulatory path is at least mapped, but 753B itself is not something a patient can be given.
risks: The VHL trick spares platelets in mice; whether it holds at active human exposures is untested
The TP53 status of the responsive primary samples is not reported, so the fit to a TP53-aberrant clone is assumed rather than shown
Blasts must express enough VHL for the degrader to work, and VHL levels in AML are not routinely measured
Degrading BCL-2 as well means the same on-target myelosuppression that venetoclax already caused here
caveats: Single-group preclinical package. The senolytic claim is a distinct hypothesis and should not be read as supporting the venetoclax-resistance argument.

intervention_label: Non-rezatapopt Y220C chemotypes: covalent azaindoles (KG13) and the PK7088/PK9318 carbazole stabiliser series
mechanism: The Y220C substitution opens a surface crevice next to a free cysteine. The carbazole series occupies that crevice non-covalently and raises the melting temperature of the mutant protein; KG13 instead reacts covalently with the mutant cysteine, which locks in wild-type thermal stability with a different selectivity logic.
rationale: Rezatapopt is the only Y220C reactivator with a myeloid clinical program, and the upstream files already carry it. If her variant turns out to be Y220C and rezatapopt is unavailable, fails, or is refused on the AML-specific combination dependency, there are two structurally distinct chemical routes to the same pocket sitting in the academic literature. Both are early: KG13 has crystallographic and thermal-stability data, the carbazole series has cellular p53 signalling restoration in a liver-cancer line. Neither has been tested in a myeloid model.
novelty: Chemical probes with no development program, no IND and no registered trial; rezatapopt and eprenetapopt are the only p53-directed agents in trials.jsonl and clinical_evidence.jsonl.

key_manuscripts.finding: A covalent screen found small molecules that react selectively with the cysteine created by Y220C and restore wild-type thermal stability of the p53 core domain, with a 1.7 A structure of the KG13 adduct.

PK7088 raised the amount of correctly folded Y220C protein in cells and restored p53 target-gene transcription, growth arrest and apoptosis in a Y220C-dependent way. Later analogues in the same series pushed affinity into the single-digit micromolar range.

model_systems: recombinant p53 DNA-binding domain (thermal stability, crystallography)
developability: Structure-biology probes. Neither series has cell-line-level potency good enough to justify IND work, and neither has been run in leukaemia cells at all.
risks: The whole idea evaporates unless the pending NGS returns Y220C specifically; a non-Y220C TP53 aberration makes these compounds inert
No myeloid model data, so the AML-specific point that reactivated p53 needs a BCL-2-family partner to actually kill is untested for these chemotypes
Covalent cysteine chemistry carries a proteome-selectivity burden that has not been resolved for KG13
The 2019-versus-2026 NGS discrepancy has to be settled before any of this is worth pursuing
caveats: Superseded in practice by rezatapopt wherever rezatapopt is accessible; log this as a fallback chemotype question, not a parallel option.

intervention_label: Decitabine plus an ATR inhibitor, as a TP53-mutant-selective combination
target_feature_label: TP53 aberration - replication-stress vulnerability rather than p53 reactivation
mechanism: Decitabine slows replication fork progression and produces single-strand breaks, which switches on the ATR checkpoint. TP53-mutant AML cells resolve that stress poorly, so adding an ATR inhibitor pushes them into mitotic catastrophe while TP53-wild-type cells survive.
rationale: This is the one TP53 idea on this list that does not depend on getting p53 protein working again, which matters when the variant identity is unresolved and may be a copy-loss rather than a missense. Baeten and colleagues built the effect in isogenic TP53-mutant AML cells and then showed reduced leukaemia burden and longer survival in mouse models. The oddest and most useful detail is negative: azacitidine did not do it, and neither did a potent DNMT1 inhibitor producing the same global hypomethylation, so the effect is decitabine-specific and not a methylation effect. Both components are obtainable drugs, which is unusual for this file.
novelty: Decitabine is approved and ATR inhibitors are in trials separately, but no registered study pairs them in TP53-mutant myeloid disease, and neither ATR nor a replication-stress mechanism appears anywhere in trials.jsonl, clinical_evidence.jsonl or preclinical_evidence.jsonl.

key_manuscripts.finding: Decitabine induced replication stress and ATR pathway activation, which TP53-mutant AML cells resolved poorly; adding an ATR inhibitor was selectively lethal to TP53-mutant cells through mitotic catastrophe and prolonged survival in mouse models. Azacitidine and the DNMT1 inhibitor GSK3685032 produced comparable hypomethylation but no synergy.

model_systems: in vivo mouse models of TP53-mutant AML
developability: Both halves already exist as human drugs, so this is a combination-trial question rather than a discovery question. An ATR inhibitor would still have to come through a study, and the myelosuppression of the pair in a patient with 85% marrow blasts is unknown.
risks: Her TP53 status is unconfirmed; if the 2026 negative is real, the selectivity argument does not apply
Prior hypomethylating-agent exposure during the 2019-2020 MDS phase is not documented, and decitabine refractoriness would undercut the whole combination
Overlapping myelosuppression in a heavily pretreated post-transplant marrow
Mouse marrow models say nothing about a thigh myeloid sarcoma
Effect sizes come from one group; no independent replication yet
caveats: Published April 2026, so nobody has had time to reproduce it. Treat the decitabine-versus-azacitidine distinction as the load-bearing and most fragile claim.

intervention_label: CD123-targeted degrader-antibody conjugates with a GSPT1-degrading payload (ORM-1153; Hdz-C123A)
target_feature_label: CD123+ blasts, with a payload chosen to work despite TP53 aberration
mechanism: An anti-CD123 antibody carries a cereblon-based molecular glue that degrades the translation termination factor GSPT1 once internalised. Killing therefore runs through collapse of protein synthesis rather than through DNA damage, which is where p53 would normally be needed.
rationale: The CD123 agent already on her trial list, pivekimab sunirine, delivers a DNA-alkylating payload whose death signal is p53-dependent and BCL-2-family-gated, which is exactly the wiring her disease has probably broken. Swapping the payload for a GSPT1 degrader keeps the CD123 handle and drops the p53 requirement. The sponsor reports retained potency in TP53-mutant isogenic AML lines and across primary blasts, and untargeted GSPT1 degraders had a narrow therapeutic index in AML that antibody conjugation is meant to widen. I would rank this the most likely of my candidates to become an actual trial she could reach.
novelty: The CD33-conjugated version of this idea (ORM-6151 / BMS-986497) is already enrolling and sits in trials.jsonl; the CD123-conjugated version has no registered study and no CD123 agent in the upstream files uses a p53-independent payload.

key_manuscripts.finding: ORM-1153 killed CD123-expressing AML lines and primary blasts through GSPT1 degradation and kept its potency in TP53-mutant isogenic lines, which the authors put forward as the case for genetically high-risk disease.
Follow-up characterisation of ORM-1153 covering activity across AML models and the therapeutic-index argument for conjugating a GSPT1 degrader to a CD123 antibody rather than dosing it systemically.

An independent CD123-GSPT1 degrader conjugate, Hdz-C123A, showed picomolar antiproliferative activity in CD123-expressing lines, activity in gemtuzumab-resistant lines, and in vivo efficacy with limited toxicity to healthy-donor PBMCs. Two groups converging on the same design raises confidence in the concept if not in either molecule.

developability: Furthest along of anything on this list. Regulatory submission has been signalled for the second half of 2026, so a first-in-human study is plausibly within a year, which is the wrong timescale for 82% peripheral blasts but the right one for a post-remission or post-HCT2 question.
risks: All data are conference abstracts from the sponsor; nothing is peer-reviewed and no independent group has replicated ORM-1153 specifically
Systemic GSPT1 degraders (CC-90009) caused hypotension and infusion reactions in AML trials, and antibody conjugation is an untested fix in humans
Her CD123 is qualitative flow only; antigen density, which drives payload delivery, is unmeasured
Whether an ADC reaches a thigh myeloid sarcoma at cytotoxic concentrations is unknown for any CD123 agent
No trial exists yet, so this cannot be accessed today
caveats: The TP53-independence claim rests on isogenic cell lines, not on TP53-aberrant patient material.

intervention_label: Multiplex epitope-edited donor HSPC graft (CD123 / FLT3 / KIT), shielding normal haematopoiesis from antigen-directed therapy
target_feature_label: CD123+ / CD33+ blasts, with the donor graft engineered to tolerate antigen-directed therapy
mechanism: Base editing changes a handful of residues in the antibody epitope of CD123, FLT3 or KIT on donor stem cells without disturbing protein function or signalling. Edited haematopoiesis then survives a CAR-T or antibody aimed at the unedited version of the antigen, so the antigen-directed agent can be dosed to leukaemia-clearing levels.
rationale: The recurring problem with her two confirmed handles is that CD123 and CD33 are shared with normal myeloid progenitors, which is what caps every CD123 and CD33 agent on the trial list. If a second transplant happens, the graft is the natural place to solve that, and the same platform underwrites post-transplant antigen-directed consolidation rather than competing with it. Casirati's group edited all three antigens at up to 75-90% efficiency and eradicated AML in mice while dual-edited human cells survived bispecific CAR-T pressure. Editing does not touch the leukaemia, so it only helps if a competent antigen-directed agent is available at the same time.
novelty: The single-gene CD33-edited graft (trem-cel) has reached the clinic; multiplex CD123/FLT3/KIT editing has no IND, and no epitope-editing strategy appears in trials.jsonl, clinical_evidence.jsonl or preclinical_evidence.jsonl.

key_manuscripts.finding: Base editing of the targeted epitope on FLT3, KIT and CD123 in human HSPCs reached up to 90%, 85% and 75% efficiency, single or multiplexed, without altering protein function. Dual-edited FLT3/CD123 cells survived a bispecific CAR-T that cleared AML from the tested tissues.

An independent group engineered the CD123 epitope in human HSPCs and showed the edited cells were shielded from CD123-directed immunotherapy while retaining normal differentiation. Useful mainly because it is a second lab reaching the same conclusion on the CD123 arm.

The original demonstration that CD33-deleted donor stem cells reconstitute normal haematopoiesis and tolerate CD33-directed CAR-T, which is the proof of concept the whole field is built on. Note the 2019 published correction attached to this paper.

developability: The CD33 single-edit version proved the manufacturing and regulatory path is walkable, which is the strongest argument for the multiplex version. Still needs an IND, a paired antigen-directed agent, and a donor willing and able to give cells a second time.
risks: Requires a second transplant to be feasible at all, which is its own unresolved question here
Base editing carries bystander-edit and off-target liabilities that are managed, not eliminated
Manufacturing timelines are weeks; her peripheral blasts went 58% to 82% in about a month
The shield is only useful paired with a CD123 or CD33 agent dosed above current tolerability, and no such agent is approved
Editing three antigens at once has not been taken into any human
caveats: This is a platform, not a drug. Its value here is entirely contingent on the HCT2 decision going forward.

intervention_label: CD33 C2-set-domain-directed binders and CAR T cells (CD33 PAN antibodies)
target_feature_label: CD33+ blasts with unmeasured density and unknown rs12459419 splice genotype
mechanism: Every CD33 agent in clinical use binds the membrane-distal V-set domain, which is the part that disappears when the rs12459419 splicing SNP drives exon-2 skipping. Binders raised against the membrane-proximal C2-set domain recognise CD33 whether or not the V-set domain is present, and the shorter binding distance also excludes CD45 from the immune synapse, which sharpens CAR T-cell signalling.
rationale: Her CD33 is qualitative flow only, her rs12459419 genotype is unknown, and the profile explicitly asks for quantitative antigen density before committing to CD33-directed therapy. A C2-directed binder makes the splice genotype irrelevant and lowers the density needed to fire the receptor, so it answers two of the open questions at once. Walter's group raised the antibodies and then built CAR T cells on them, with the expected specificity in engineered lines. The catch is that this is a Fred Hutch research program, not a product.
novelty: All CD33 agents in trials.jsonl (gemtuzumab ozogamicin, lintuzumab-Ac225, CD33 CAR-T, GTB-3650, BMS-986497) are V-set binders; no C2-directed CD33 construct appears in any upstream file and none has an IND.

key_manuscripts.finding: Antibodies raised against the C2-set domain bound CD33 regardless of whether the V-set domain was present, which makes them independent of the rs12459419 splice genotype that governs gemtuzumab benefit.

CAR T cells built on the C2-directed binders killed CD33-expressing targets with the expected domain specificity, and the membrane-proximal epitope gave better synapse geometry than V-set-directed constructs.

model_systems: engineered CD33-isoform ML-1 and REH lines
developability: Academic constructs with no clinical-grade vector or IND. A C2-directed bispecific did reach phase 1 elsewhere (JNJ-67571244) and was discontinued, so the epitope itself is not untested in humans even though this CAR is.
risks: Changing epitope does not change the total amount of CD33 on the blast, so a genuinely CD33-low clone still resists
CD33 CAR T cells carry the same prolonged myelotoxicity as every other on-target-off-tumour myeloid CAR
No clinical-grade C2-directed CAR product exists anywhere
The companion argument about the exon-2-deleted isoform being a target does not hold up (see the considered_excluded row), so the case rests on density and synapse geometry alone
caveats: Worth logging mainly as a reason to obtain the quantitative CD33 flow and rs12459419 genotype the profile already asks for.

intervention_label: EZH2 PROTAC degrader (MS177 class) to reverse non-genomic HLA class II silencing at post-transplant relapse
target_feature_label: Post-transplant immune escape upstream of any HLA-restricted cellular therapy
mechanism: MS177 pulls EZH2 to cereblon and degrades it, taking down both the canonical EZH2-PRC2 complex and the non-canonical EZH2-cMyc complex that catalytic inhibitors leave running. Removing the protein rather than blocking the SET domain reopens PRC2-closed loci faster and, in the myeloma work, switched on interferon-gamma response and MHC antigen-processing genes.
rationale: Her relapse six years after a matched-sibling transplant looks like graft-versus-leukaemia escape rather than graft failure, and her flow shows HLA-DR variably decreased. The researcher tier already carries the argument that class II loss at post-transplant relapse is PRC2-enforced and pharmacologically reversible. What is not covered is that catalytic EZH2 inhibition is slow and leaves the non-canonical arm intact, which is the specific gap degraders were built for. Restoring antigen presentation before, not after, giving donor cells is the sequencing question worth asking.
novelty: Catalytic PRC2 inhibition is what preclinical_evidence carries and what the approved EZH2 inhibitors do; no EZH2 degrader has an IND, and none appears in any upstream file.

key_manuscripts.finding: EZH2 has a hidden transactivation domain that binds cMyc and p300 at non-PRC2 targets, which explains why catalytic inhibitors act slowly. The PROTAC MS177 depleted both complexes and suppressed acute leukaemia growth faster and more potently than enzymatic inhibition.

In myeloma, MS177 but not the matched catalytic inhibitor turned on interferon-gamma response and MHC antigen processing and presentation programs. This is the only direct evidence that degradation, specifically, reopens antigen presentation.

EZH2-driven MHC class II silencing defined a high-risk acute leukaemia subset, and combining an EZH2 inhibitor with interferon-gamma reversed the immune-evasion phenotype in FUS::ERG AML cells. A preprint, in a different AML subtype, and using the inhibitor rather than a degrader.

developability: No EZH2 degrader has entered IND-enabling development. The nearest accessible substitute is an approved catalytic EZH2 inhibitor, which the researcher tier already covers and which the degrader work argues is the weaker tool.
risks: EZH2 sits at 7q36.1 and this patient carries del(7q), so the gene may already be hemizygous. Degrading what is left could push in the wrong direction, since EZH2 loss behaves as a myeloid tumour suppressor
Nobody has measured whether her blasts have actually lost HLA class II; 'HLA-DR variably decreased' on a diagnostic flow panel is not that measurement
The class II restoration evidence is myeloma transcriptomics plus a preprint in a different AML subtype, not post-transplant relapse material
Reopening antigen presentation without a donor effector population present does nothing, so this only makes sense bolted to DLI or a second transplant
Restoring class II would also raise the graft-versus-host disease risk it is trying to exploit
caveats: The del(7q) tension is the reason I have this at speculative rather than emerging; it is a real possibility that this patient is the wrong patient for this mechanism.

intervention_label: Whole-exome minor-histocompatibility-antigen mapping of this recipient/sibling-donor pair to nominate non-HA-1 GvL targets
target_feature_label: HLA-restricted immunotherapy handles, where HLA-A*02:01 status is unknown
mechanism: Whole-exome sequencing of germline DNA from both donor and recipient finds the coding polymorphisms where they differ, then class I binding prediction, ligandome detection and expression filtering narrow those to peptides a donor T cell could see on haematopoietic tissue. The output is a ranked list of candidate GvL targets restricted to whatever HLA alleles this pair actually carries.
rationale: Every cellular option this case was submitted for (HA-1, HA-2, WT1-C4, PRAME) is gated on HLA-A*02:01, which nobody has retrieved. If that allele comes back negative the entire stack collapses at once, and the fallback in the profile is a single A*24:02-restricted WT1 product. Cieri and colleagues built and validated a pipeline that does this systematically across 220 HLA-matched pairs and identified GvL targets in a validation cohort. Running it on this specific sibling pair converts a binary eligibility question into a search, which seems worth doing in parallel with the HLA retrieval rather than after it.
novelty: The upstream files carry specific mHAg products (TSC-100/101, MDG1021, BSB-1001, GLIDE) but no strategy for finding targets when the pair does not fit those products; the discovery pipeline itself has no clinical program.

key_manuscripts.finding: An integrated pipeline combining donor-recipient whole-exome sequencing, class I ligandome detection and expression filtering identified mHAgs across 220 HLA-matched transplant pairs; total and organ-specific mHAg load independently predicted acute and chronic pulmonary GvHD, and the method nominated GvL targets confirmed in a 58-pair validation cohort.

developability: The sequencing and prediction half is a service anyone with stored donor and recipient DNA could commission. The gap is on the other side: a nominated mHAg is not a product, and building a TCR against a bespoke target takes years, so realistically this informs eligibility and donor selection rather than delivering a therapy.
risks: Requires retrievable germline DNA from the 2020 sibling donor, which may not exist
A nominated antigen with broad tissue expression drives graft-versus-host disease rather than graft-versus-leukaemia, and the expression filter is imperfect
Discovery timelines do not match a patient whose peripheral blasts went 58% to 82% in a month
The published work predicts outcomes and nominates targets; it does not show that a nominated target was successfully drugged
Escape by antigen loss or class I downregulation applies here exactly as it does to HA-1
caveats: Best read as a decision-support move that runs alongside HLA retrieval, not as a candidate therapy.

intervention_label: DRP1 inhibition (Mdivi-1) to restore venetoclax-induced mitochondrial apoptosis in TP53-mutant AML
mechanism: Blocking the mitochondrial fission GTPase DRP1 shifts mitochondrial morphology in a way that lowers the threshold for BAX and BAK activation, which the authors report restores venetoclax-driven outer-membrane permeabilisation in TP53-mutant cells.
rationale: It targets the same broken effector layer as the BAX-activator idea but from the mitochondrial-dynamics side, and Mdivi-1 is a cheap and widely available tool compound. I am including it because the mechanism is on-axis for a TP53-aberrant venetoclax failure, and excluding it would hide a direction someone might reasonably want to chase. I would not put much weight on it: one paper, cell lines only, and Mdivi-1's selectivity for DRP1 has been questioned in the wider literature.
novelty: Mitochondrial-dynamics targeting appears nowhere in the upstream files, and no DRP1 inhibitor has a registered oncology trial in any indication.

key_manuscripts.finding: DRP1 inhibition enhanced venetoclax-induced mitochondrial apoptosis in TP53-mutated AML cell lines through BAX/BAK activation. Cell lines only, no animal data, and no independent replication that I could find.

developability: Mdivi-1 is a laboratory reagent, not a drug. There is no clinical-grade DRP1 inhibitor and no obvious sponsor for one.
risks: Rests on a single in-vitro paper with no in-vivo confirmation and no independent replication
Mdivi-1's specificity has been challenged; some of its cellular effects have been attributed to complex I inhibition rather than DRP1
The premise is re-challenging with venetoclax after documented progression, which is a weak starting point clinically
Mitochondrial fission machinery is essential in normal tissue, and the therapeutic window is uncharacterised
caveats: Included for completeness of the apoptosis-restoration axis. If the preclinical_reporter ranks this above the BAX or BCL-xL rows, something has gone wrong.

intervention_label: EVI1-CTBP1/2 PLDLS interaction inhibitor (4x PLDLS decoy construct)
target_feature_label: MECOM/EVI1 gain at relapse (nominal target mapping only)
mechanism: EVI1 needs a single PLDLS motif to recruit CTBP1 and CTBP2, and that interaction is required for leukaemic transformation. A four-copy PLDLS decoy outcompetes the binding and stalls 3q26/MECOM-rearranged AML in vitro and in xenografts.
rationale: Her 2026 relapse karyotype carries a 5' MECOM gain, which is an adverse driver with no conventional handle, so I scanned specifically for whether EVI1 had become druggable since the previous run on this case.
exclusion_reason: MECOM/EVI1 is not among profile.json::targetable_features[], and the EVI1-CTBP2 mechanism does not route through CD123, CD33, TP53, the HLA-restricted handles or the transplant platform (the targets field here is a nominal placeholder). The proof of concept is also a genetically delivered peptide decoy rather than a molecule anyone could dose, and the published work is in 3q26-rearranged AML, not MECOM gain. Recording it so the audit trail shows the direction was checked and where it stands.

key_manuscripts.finding: A 4x PLDLS repeat construct displaced EVI1 from CTBP1/2 and inhibited proliferation of 3q26/MECOM-rearranged AML in vitro and in xenotransplant models, which is the first credible target for this otherwise undrugged transcription factor.

intervention_label: Collateral-lethality strategies keyed to hemizygous 7q loss (EED, BRD4 and the 27-gene synthetic-lethal set)
mechanism: Hemizygous deletion leaves a set of genes at half dosage, and knocking down the remaining copy is tolerated by normal cells but not by the deleted clone. Systematic analysis of over 600 -7/del(7q) samples narrowed this to roughly 27 candidate genes; separate screens put EED and BRD4 forward.
rationale: del(7q) is one of her founder lesions and persists across both timepoints, so a dosage-based vulnerability would be clone-selective in a way nothing else on this list is.
exclusion_reason: del(7q) is not among the stated targetable_features (the targets field is a nominal placeholder), and the two nominated genes are hit by drug classes already enrolling patients: BET inhibitors for BRD4 and PRC2-directed agents for EED. The same analysis explicitly argues CUX1 and EZH2 are poor synthetic-lethal candidates because loss-of-function cases exist. There is no compound here that is both on-target and earlier than clinical development.

key_manuscripts.finding: Multimodal analysis of more than 600 -7/del(7q) myeloid neoplasm samples nominated 27 candidate synthetic-lethal genes and argued against CUX1 and EZH2 as targets because hemizygous and homozygous loss-of-function cases occur.

intervention_label: Selective CK1alpha molecular glue degraders (SJ3149 series) for del(5q) CSNK1A1 haploinsufficiency
target_feature_label: del(5q) CSNK1A1 haploinsufficiency (nominal target mapping only)
mechanism: CSNK1A1 sits at 5q32, so del(5q) cells carry one copy and are unusually sensitive to further CK1alpha loss. SJ3149 and related cereblon glues degrade CK1alpha selectively, without the IKZF1/IKZF3 co-degradation that lenalidomide brings.
rationale: del(5q) is her other founder lesion and CK1alpha haploinsufficiency is the best-characterised dosage vulnerability in myeloid disease, so it was worth checking whether a selective degrader had appeared.
exclusion_reason: Two reasons. del(5q) is not among the stated targetable_features (the targets field is nominal), and more importantly the mechanism runs the wrong way for this patient: CK1alpha degradation kills largely by stabilising p53, which is precisely the arm a TP53-aberrant clone has already lost. Pursuing it here would be counter-productive rather than merely off-scope.

key_manuscripts.finding: Structure-guided optimisation produced SJ3149, a potent and selective CK1alpha degrader active in vitro and in vivo across a broad cancer cell line panel, with activity substantially dependent on downstream p53 stabilisation.

intervention_label: RAS-pathway inhibition directed at the extramedullary myeloid sarcoma compartment
target_feature_label: Extramedullary myeloid sarcoma biology (nominal target mapping only)
mechanism: Single-cell and spatial profiling of myeloid sarcoma finds RAS-pathway mutations enriched at extramedullary sites relative to paired marrow, with RAS/ERK activation present even without a mutation, and RAS inhibition active in a murine myeloid sarcoma model.
rationale: Her right-thigh myeloid sarcoma is the compartment most likely to be missed by marrow-directed therapy, so a sanctuary-site-specific vulnerability would matter a great deal if it were real and on-feature.
exclusion_reason: The RAS pathway is not among the stated targetable_features (nominal targets mapping), no RAS or MAPK lesion was reported on either her 2019 or 2026 panels, and RAS and MEK inhibitors are clinical-stage agents that belong to trial_screener. The supporting work is also a December 2025 preprint that has not been peer-reviewed.

key_manuscripts.finding: Bulk, single-cell and spatial profiling of paired extramedullary and marrow samples showed separate clonal evolution with increased mutational burden and RAS-pathway addiction at extramedullary sites, plus efficacy of RAS inhibition in a murine model.

target_feature_label: CD123+ blasts - innate-effector hedge against T-cell exhaustion post-transplant
mechanism: Multispecific engagers cross-link CD123 on blasts to NKp46 and CD16a on NK cells, redirecting innate cytotoxicity without needing a functional autologous T-cell compartment.
rationale: On-mechanism for her CD123 handle and attractive post-transplant, where donor NK reconstitution precedes T-cell recovery, which is why it was scanned.
exclusion_reason: Already clinical-stage and therefore trial_screener's territory rather than the preclinical horizon. SAR443579/IPH6101 has run a phase 1/2 first-in-human study in relapsed/refractory AML with reported complete remissions, and AFM28 has entered phase 1. Both sit above the earlier-than-clinical bar this file is bounded to.

intervention_label: DT2216, a VHL-recruiting BCL-xL-selective PROTAC degrader
target_feature_label: Compensatory BCL2L1 reliance after venetoclax failure
mechanism: DT2216 recruits BCL-xL to VHL for degradation, sparing platelets because platelets do not express VHL. Same design logic as 753B but without the BCL-2 arm.
rationale: Directly on-mechanism for the BCL2L1 dependence that follows TP53/BAX/PMAIP1 loss, so it came up on the same searches as 753B.
exclusion_reason: Already in first-in-human study, so it belongs to trial_screener rather than here. Kept as an excluded row because it is the reason the 753B entry is written as the horizon candidate: 753B degrades BCL-xL more potently than DT2216 and adds BCL-2, and has no IND.

intervention_label: Antibodies directed at the exon-2-deleted CD33 isoform (CD33delE2)
target_feature_label: CD33+ blasts - the rs12459419 splice-escape hypothesis
mechanism: The rs12459419 splicing SNP drives skipping of CD33 exon 2, removing the V-set domain that every clinical CD33 agent binds. The idea was to raise binders against the truncated isoform so the escape variant becomes a target in its own right.
rationale: Attractive on paper for a patient whose CD33 is qualitative-only and whose splice genotype is unknown, which is why I chased it before settling on the C2-domain approach instead.
exclusion_reason: The primary data do not support the target. Godwin and Laszlo raised two antibodies (11D5, 13E11) that bound CD33delE2 on engineered lines but detected no surface CD33delE2 protein on any AML cell line or on primary blasts from 21 patients, and concluded the isoform is not a viable therapeutic target. The transcript appears not to reach the membrane. Logged so the negative result is on record rather than rediscovered.

key_manuscripts.finding: Isoform-specific antibodies confirmed CD33delE2 mRNA is widespread but found no cell-surface CD33delE2 protein in AML lines or primary samples, arguing against it as a therapeutic target.
